body_long:
Mandarin Oriental, Paris has begun a full transformation of the hotel on rue Saint-Honoré. Works started at the end of October 2026 and are being carried out in phases, so that the hotel stays fully open throughout. No completion date has been published.

## The scope

The programme covers the whole property: all rooms and suites and their bathrooms, the public spaces, the spa and every dining venue. London-based architect Tara Bernerd is redesigning the rooms, suites and public areas. Humbert & Poyet is designing three new food and beverage concepts, each overlooking the hotel's inner garden: a new bar, a brasserie-style restaurant and a refined gourmet restaurant. The aim, according to the group, is to capture the spirit of Paris with an emphasis on craftsmanship and detail.

The hotel currently counts around 135 rooms and suites, Camélia for all-day dining, the Cake Shop, a cocktail bar, and a spa with an indoor pool.

## A new general manager

The transformation is led by Vincent Poulingue, general manager since 18 May 2026. He arrived from Hôtel du Palais in Biarritz, after more than two decades in luxury hospitality with Hyatt's The Unbound Collection, IHG and Barrière in France, Portugal, Switzerland and French Polynesia. He holds an MBA from IMHI, the programme run by Cornell and ESSEC, and reports to Philippe Kronberg, area vice-president, operations.

Group chief executive Laurent Kleitman said the investment reflects the group's commitment to make the hotel one of the most distinctive addresses in Paris. The renovation is part of the group's ten-year strategy, which focuses on renewing existing hotels and expanding in key global cities.

## The signal

Renovating a palace without closing it is one of the hardest exercises in luxury hotel management: works have to be invisible to guests while the product changes around them. Mandarin Oriental, Paris will be a live case study for every Paris general manager planning a renovation in the coming years.

Congratulations to Vincent Poulingue and his team on this new chapter.
summary: Rooms and suites are being redesigned by Tara Bernerd and three new dining concepts by Humbert & Poyet. GM Vincent Poulingue has been in post since 18 May. No completion date published.
